intent: A ranked list: each row shows a label and its value, with a quiet horizontal bar behind the label sized against the largest value. Top rows first, with Show all for the rest.
useWhen: Top items by one measure in a side column or card, like top pages by views or top customers by revenue
A short ranking where people read the exact value of each row, and rows may open the item they name
A breakdown that is too long or too narrow for an axis chart
doNotUseWhen: Several series, an axis, gridlines or a table view — use BarChart
Usage against a plan limit, with near-limit warnings — use UsageList
Part of a whole for a handful of segments — use PieChart
Records with avatars, actions or selection — use ListView
Values compared across several columns — use Table or DataTable

label.note: What the row is. Labels are the row keys, so keep them unique.

value.note: Zero or more. The bar is sized against the largest value in data, shown or not.

href.note: Makes the label a link to the item it names.

data.note: One row per item, in any order: sort decides the order shown. An empty array shows No data.

sort.note: descending puts the largest first; none keeps the order of data.

maxRows.note: Rows shown before Show all. Without it every row shows. Show all appears only when data has more rows than maxRows, and it turns into Show fewer once open.

valueFormatter.note: (value: number) => string for the value text, like a currency or a percent. Defaults to the chart format: 1,240, 12.4k, 1.2M.

label.note: Names the list for screen readers, like Top pages by views. The visible title comes from a parent Section or Card.

requirements: An ordered list named by label, so the rank and the number of rows are read
Each row reads its label and its value as text; the bar is decoration and hidden from screen readers
A row with href is one link, reachable with Tab, with a visible focus ring
Show all is a kit Button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the list, and focus stays on it when rows open or close

doNot: Do not use it for several series or an axis — use BarChart
Do not use it for usage against a limit — use UsageList
Do not build ranked rows from ListView, Table or loose bars and text — use BarList
Do not colour single rows to mean good or bad; it is one measure in one colour
Do not pass negative values; bars start at zero
Do not put it in a Card and a Section at once, or draw a box around it yourself. The title comes from a parent Section or Card
Do not use raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps
snippet:
<Section title="Top pages">
  <BarList
    label="Top pages by views"
    maxRows={5}
    data={[
      { label: "/pricing", value: 4820, href: "/analytics/pricing" },
      { label: "/docs/install", value: 3110 },
      { label: "/blog/launch", value: 1960 },
    ]}
  />
</Section>
